args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) covers the failure, the rollback and the result after it. Opening it paged the on-call engineer. Its next step is to find out what broke in v2.3.1 before it goes out again.

The test build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) also failed its health checks in staging, but v2.3.1 was still deployed to production. Someone should look at why it wasn't stopped before release.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
